This chapter introduces the DREI framework and walks through its key analytical components.

The lessons are organised to progressively build understanding of the methodology and how it supports investment planning for renewable energy.

Lesson 1: Introduction to the DREI Framework
Provides an overview of the origins, structure, and purpose of the DREI framework, and introduces the types of applications it has supported across different technologies and contexts.

Lesson 2: Risk Environment
Covers how the risk environment for renewable energy investment is assessed.

This includes stakeholder engagement, structured interviews, and financing cost analysis using the Financing Costs Waterfall.

Lesson 3: Public Instruments
Introduces the identification and evaluation of public derisking instruments.

It shows how these instruments can reduce the cost of capital and presents the post-derisking waterfall to estimate their potential impact.

Lesson 4: LCOE Modelling
Explains how the levelized cost of electricity 💬️ (LCOE) is calculated for both renewable and baseline technologies, and how changes in financing conditions influence cost competitiveness.
Chapter 3 introduces the key components of the Derisking Renewable Energy Investment (DREI) framework and its application process.

It begins with a presentation of the framework’s origins and evolution, followed by a series of lessons that reflect the main analytical building blocks of DREI: assessing the risk environment, identifying public instruments, estimating the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), and exploring scenario-based sensitivities.
To support understanding, the chapter includes illustrative applications of the DREI methodology.
These examples demonstrate how the framework can be used to analyse investment conditions and design targeted public interventions across different renewable energy technologies and country contexts.
Each lesson combines conceptual elements with methodological guidance, offering a structured introduction to how DREI supports renewable energy investment planning.
